A 39-year-old woman from Heywood has been arrested following a violent incident at Milnrow Cricket Club on April 2. Tara Hulme, known for her TikTok presence under the handle 'Heffer2020', was reportedly found drunkenly slumped in her seat at the club, prompting staff to ask her to leave.

According to Tameside Magistrates' Court, after being asked to exit the premises, Hulme became aggressive, slapping the bar manageress and spitting at two other staff members. The court heard that she also kicked a barmaid in the knee and punched another woman outside the pavilion, causing visible injury.

The incident escalated when a male club member intervened to stop the violence. Witnesses reported that families, including children, were present during the altercation, raising concerns about the safety of patrons at the family-friendly venue. One victim expressed feeling vulnerable and shocked by the incident, particularly given that it occurred in a workplace setting.

Hulme has a history of violence, with 19 previous offences, including an assault conviction from 2009. During the court proceedings, she claimed to have a 'vague' recollection of the events. The case highlights ongoing concerns regarding public safety in community spaces, particularly where families gather.

articles.title: Rochdale Health Leaders Present Collaborative Care Model at European Conference
articles.excerpt: Health leaders from Rochdale showcased their integrated healthcare model at an international conference in Belgium, highlighting the importance of collaboration in improving patient care.
articles.content_html:
Health leaders from Rochdale, Greater Manchester, presented their collaborative working model at the International Conference on Integrated Care held in Antwerp, Belgium. The event attracted over 1,000 delegates, where they shared insights on improving health and social care services.

Dr Salman Shahid, Associate Medical Director of the Greater Manchester Integrated Care Board, led the presentation alongside a team from One Rochdale Health and Care. They focused on the 'Integration Continuum' and its role in achieving patient-centred care within an integrated healthcare framework.

During the conference, Dr Shahid emphasised the need for a multi-disciplinary approach to tackle health inequalities in Rochdale, which is one of ten areas in Greater Manchester facing significant challenges. He noted the importance of collaboration among hospitals, community services, GP practices, and voluntary organisations to enhance patient and public involvement in health services.

Dr Shahid, along with colleagues Dr Kirsty Marshall, Dr Shona McCallum, and Alison Kelly, highlighted their work on improving patient engagement in health and social care. They discussed how their integrated approach aims to create a seamless health and well-being model with shared responsibility for patient care.

The conference provided an opportunity for Rochdale's health leaders to learn from colleagues across Europe, aiming to refine their approaches and ultimately improve the health and well-being of residents in the region. Dr Shahid stated that the insights gained would help enhance their systems and create a better health and social care framework for local residents.

articles.title: Egerton Street Roadworks in Heywood Scheduled from 20 October 2026
articles.excerpt: Roadworks on Egerton Street in Heywood will result in a temporary closure from 20 October to 1 November 2026, affecting traffic flow in the area.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has announced that part of Egerton Street in Heywood will be temporarily closed for roadworks from midnight on Tuesday, 20 October 2026, until 11.59pm on Sunday, 1 November 2026. The closure will extend from the junction with Hind Hill Street and will continue 165 metres west along Egerton Street.

During this period, no waiting will be permitted in the closed section of the road. The roadworks are expected to impact traffic flow, particularly affecting routes through Hind Hill Street, Market Place, York Street, Bamford Road, Market Street, Dawson Street, Bridge Street, and Pilsworth Road.

Motorists are advised to plan their journeys accordingly and consider alternative routes during the closure. The council has provided a map of the roadworks and other restrictions across Greater Manchester, which can be accessed through their website.

Further updates regarding the progress of the roadworks and any changes to the schedule will be communicated by Rochdale Borough Council as the work commences.

articles.title: Rochdale Town Hall Renovation Wins Europa Nostra Award
articles.excerpt: The renovation of Rochdale Town Hall has received the prestigious Europa Nostra award, recognising its excellence in heritage conservation following a £20 million restoration project.
articles.content_html:
The renovation of Rochdale Town Hall has been honoured with the Europa Nostra award, one of Europe’s most prestigious accolades for heritage conservation. This award comes as part of a series of recognitions for the Grade I-listed building, which reopened fully last year after a £20 million restoration project.

The Europa Nostra award is particularly significant, as it was awarded to only three projects out of 261 applications across Europe. This latest accolade complements previous honours for the town hall, including the Civic Trust Awards, where it received the Michael Middleton Special Award for Excellence in Conservation and a Civic Trust Conservation Award.

In June 2026, the project also garnered four awards at the Royal Institute of British Architects (RIBA) North West Awards, including the RIBA North West Award 2026 and the RIBA North West Project Architect of the Year 2026. Additionally, it was recognised as the Social Project of the Year at the Association for Project Management (APM) Awards 2025, highlighting its positive impact on the community and economy.

The ongoing recognition of Rochdale Town Hall's renovation underscores its importance not only as a historical landmark but also as a centre for community engagement and cultural heritage. The town hall continues to serve as a venue for various events and activities, contributing to the local community's vibrancy.

articles.title: Rochdale Opens Fourth Children's Home 'Diamond' to Support Young People
articles.excerpt: Rochdale Borough Council has opened its fourth children's home, named 'Diamond', as part of a £3.4 million investment to provide care for children with complex needs.
articles.content_html:
Rochdale Borough Council has officially opened its fourth children's home, named 'Diamond', as part of a £3.4 million investment aimed at expanding residential care provision for children in the borough. This new facility will support three children with complex needs and disabilities who come into care, featuring a dedicated sensory room designed to enhance their living experience.

The opening of Diamond marks the completion of a quartet of new homes, which also includes homes named Emerald, Sapphire, and Ruby. These names were chosen following suggestions from children in care, reflecting their input in the development process. In total, the new homes provide 12 placements, allowing more children to remain within their local community rather than being placed far from home.

Councillor Rachel Massey, cabinet member for children's services and education, expressed her delight at the opening, stating that Diamond will offer a homely and friendly environment that can significantly improve the lives of children and young people in need of support. This initiative comes at a time when local councils face challenges in finding suitable placements for children in care, making the establishment of these homes particularly significant.

The new children's home is expected to provide a warm and comforting environment for its residents, ensuring that they can stay close to their families and communities. The council's investment in these facilities is a proactive step towards addressing the ongoing need for local care options for vulnerable children.

articles.title: Peacocks to Open New Store at Rochdale Riverside as Footfall Increases by 15.3%
articles.excerpt: British clothing retailer Peacocks has signed a long-term lease for a unit at Rochdale Riverside, contributing to a 15.3% rise in footfall at the shopping centre.
articles.content_html:
British clothing retailer Peacocks has secured a long-term lease for a 10,181 sq ft unit at Rochdale Riverside, which is now 92% occupied. The store is set to open at the beginning of October 2026, further enhancing the shopping and leisure offerings at the centre.

The announcement follows a significant 15.3% increase in footfall at Rochdale Riverside, with nearly 200,000 visitors recorded in July alone. This upward trend in visitor numbers has been consistent throughout 2026, indicating a growing interest in the retail destination since its opening in Spring 2020.

Rochdale Riverside, which spans 200,000 sq ft, features a mix of shopping, dining, and leisure options, anchored by a 50,000 sq ft Marks & Spencer store and a six-screen Real Cinema. Other national retailers at the centre include Next, H&M, Boots, and JD Sports. Ollie Holland, asset manager for Rochdale Riverside at RivingtonHark, expressed confidence in the centre's appeal, stating that the addition of Peacocks reflects strong demand for well-located retail space.

Councillor Danny Meredith, cabinet member for regeneration and housing at Rochdale Borough Council, welcomed the new store, noting that it would be a popular addition to the shopping centre. Peacocks, established in 1884 and now operating 345 stores across the UK, is known for its budget-friendly clothing options, which will complement the existing retail mix at Rochdale Riverside.

articles.title: Failsworth Tram Stop Lift Out of Service Due to Replacement Works
articles.excerpt: The lift at Failsworth Tram Stop is currently out of service, affecting access for passengers. Those needing step-free access should travel to Hollinwood.
articles.content_html:
The lift at Failsworth Tram Stop, which services the platform heading towards Rochdale, is currently out of service due to replacement works. This situation has been in effect since 6:48am on Thursday, 24 September 2026, and will continue until further notice.

As a result of the lift being out of service, there is no step-free access available at this stop. Passengers requiring step-free access are advised to make their way to Hollinwood Tram Stop to connect to services.

Customers needing assistance or additional journey planning support are encouraged to contact the Metrolink customer service centre at 0161 244 1000. The lines are open from 7am to 8pm on weekdays and from 8am to 8pm on weekends and Bank Holidays.

This disruption may affect local commuters and those travelling to and from Rochdale, so passengers should plan their journeys accordingly.

articles.title: Ofsted Inspection Report Published for Little Miracles Daycare in Rochdale
articles.excerpt: Ofsted has released a new inspection report for Little Miracles Daycare, detailing the findings and rating awarded to the childcare provider in Rochdale.
articles.content_html:
Ofsted has published a new inspection report for Little Miracles Daycare, a childcare provider in Rochdale. The report, dated 24 September 2026, outlines the findings from the recent inspection and the rating awarded to the setting.

According to Ofsted, settings registered on the Early Years Register are typically inspected at least once within a four-year period. Inspections may occur more frequently if there are concerns, and newly registered settings are inspected within 18 months of their registration. Compliance inspections are also conducted for settings registered on the Childcare Register.

The report provides insights into the quality of care and education provided at Little Miracles Daycare, which is essential for parents seeking reliable childcare options in the area. Families can access the report online to better understand the standards met by the daycare.

For those interested in further details or to compare other childcare providers, Ofsted encourages visiting their website. Parents can also subscribe to alerts for future reports on this provider.
